journey.title: Tab out of the departure date to the passengers field
journey.goal: Tab moves focus from the date field to the next field, as in any form

functionalJourney.title: Change the passengers with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Editing another field and saving submits the saved departure date

guards.title: Escape still closes the calendar
guards.goal: With the calendar open, Escape closes it and Tab then reaches the passengers field

plan.root_cause: The Tab key's default action is prevented when the datepicker is open, preventing focus from moving to the next form field. This occurs because the datepicker component does not handle the Tab key to close itself, allowing the Vanilla Calendar Pro library to trap focus and prevent Tab navigation.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a keydown listener to the document that hides the datepicker when the Tab key is pressed and the datepicker is shown. This allows the Tab key's default action to proceed, moving focus to the next form field. The listener is added in _setupDismiss and cleaned up in dispose, with the corresponding property declaration added to the class.

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Tab from the departure date field will move focus to the passengers field, restoring the expected form navigation order for keyboard users.
functional_risks: The datepicker may close unexpectedly when navigating within the calendar using the Tab key, if the Vanilla Calendar Pro library supports Tab navigation internally.

If the datepicker is open and the user presses Tab to move focus to an element inside the datepicker (such as a button in the calendar header), the datepicker will close and focus will leave the datepicker prematurely.
verification_requirements: Tab key press from the departure date input must move focus to the passengers input.
Escape key press must still close the datepicker and keep focus on the departure date input (as per regression guard).
The datepicker must still open when the departure date input receives focus.
Clicking outside the datepicker must still close it.

plan.root_cause: Vanilla Calendar Pro sets tabindex=-1 on the input when the calendar opens, removing it from the tab order. When Tab is pressed from the departure field, the browser cannot navigate from an element outside the tab order, so focus falls back to body instead of moving to passengers.
plan.repair_strategy: In the VCP onShow callback, restore the input's tabindex to 0 so it remains in the tab order. This allows natural Tab navigation to the next field. The existing focusin dismiss handler (_onOutside) will close the datepicker when focus moves outside.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Tab from the departure date field moves focus to the passengers field naturally, as the input remains in the tab order. The datepicker closes automatically via the existing focusin handler when focus leaves.
functional_risks: Restoring tabindex may conflict with VCP's internal focus management, but VCP's focus trapping is the root cause of the accessibility failure.
If VCP immediately resets tabindex after onShow, the fix may not persist; however, onShow fires after VCP's show logic.
verification_requirements: Tab key press from the departure date input moves focus to the passengers input.
Escape key press still closes the datepicker and keeps focus on the departure date input (regression guard).
The datepicker still opens when the departure date input receives focus.
Clicking outside the datepicker still closes it.

plan.root_cause: The Vanilla Calendar Pro library prevents the default action of the Tab key when the datepicker popup is open, trapping focus on the trigger input and preventing keyboard navigation to the next form field.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a keydown listener on the trigger input that calls stopImmediatePropagation() for the Tab key when the datepicker is shown. This prevents VCP's keydown listener from receiving the event and calling preventDefault(), allowing the browser's default Tab navigation to proceed. The existing focusin dismiss handler will close the datepicker when focus moves to the next field.

functional_risks: If VCP attaches its keydown listener to the input itself (not document), stopImmediatePropagation will also prevent other listeners on the input from running, but there are none.

If the user presses Tab while focused inside the calendar (e.g., on a calendar button), this fix does not apply because the listener is only on the trigger input. That's acceptable because the calendar should handle its own keyboard navigation.

plan.root_cause: Vanilla Calendar Pro (VCP) sets tabindex=-1 on the trigger input when the datepicker opens, removing it from the tab order, and also attaches a keydown listener that calls preventDefault() on the Tab key. This traps focus on the departure field, preventing natural keyboard navigation to the passengers field.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a capture-phase keydown listener on the trigger input (registered before VCP's listeners) that calls stopImmediatePropagation() for the Tab key when the datepicker is shown. This allows the browser's default Tab navigation to proceed. Also restore tabindex=0 in the onShow callback to keep the input in the tab order. The existing focusin dismiss handler (_onOutside) will close the datepicker when focus moves to the next field.

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Tab from the departure date input moves focus to the passengers input, restoring natural form navigation for keyboard users. The datepicker closes automatically via the existing focusin handler when focus leaves.
functional_risks: Capture-phase listener runs before VCP's bubble-phase listeners, but if VCP also uses capture phase, order depends on registration. Our listener is added after _initCalendar, so VCP's capture listeners (if any) would fire first. However, VCP typically uses bubble phase for keyboard trapping.
Restoring tabindex=0 in onShow assumes VCP sets tabindex=-1 before onShow fires. If VCP sets it after, a MutationObserver would be more robust but adds complexity.
verification_requirements: Tab key press from the departure date input moves focus to the passengers input.
Escape key press still closes the datepicker and keeps focus on the departure date input (regression guard).
The datepicker still opens when the departure date input receives focus.
Clicking outside the datepicker still closes it.
